chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about women who are riding on camels and beasts of burden; is it sufficient for them to stand beneath As-Safa and Al-Marwah? He said, 'Wherever they can see the House.'
And whoever walks between As-Safa and Al-Marwah and the time for prayer enters, he should interrupt it and pray, then return and complete the walking. Narrated.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa, one of the two hills in Mecca
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةُ: Al-Marwah, the second hill in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim performing Sa'i who is interrupted by prayer time or is riding an animal?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the flexibility of Sa'i rituals for those riding animals, specifying that visibility of the Kaaba suffices for the location of the ritual act. It further establishes the principle of interrupting non-obligatory acts of worship, such as Sa'i, to prioritize the obligatory prayer (Salat), ensuring the pilgrim resumes and completes the circuits afterward.
